```{r, panelbuilding}
#| label: build-panels
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| echo: false

# Funktion zum Erstellen der Panels
build_val_report <- function(i) {
  name_for_labels <- janitor::make_clean_names(val_dat$Analyt[[i]])
  
  output_first_part <- glue('
  ### `r val_dat$Analyt[[<<i>>]]`

    ',
  .open = "<<",
  .close = ">>")
  
  output_panel_summary <- glue(
    '
  #### Summary
  
  ```{r}
  #| label: summary-<<name_for_labels>>
  #| echo: false
  
  val_dat$summary_details[[<<i>>]] |> 
    knitr::kable()
  ```',
  .open = "<<",
  .close = ">>"
  )
  
  output_panel_plot <- glue(
    '
  #### Scatter-Plot

  ```{r}
  #| label: plot-summary-<<name_for_labels>>
  #| echo: false

  val_dat$plot[[<<i>>]]
  ```',
  .open = "<<",
  .close = ">>"
  )
  
  output_panel_paba <- glue(
    '
  #### Passing-Bablok

  ```{r}
  #| label: plot-paba-<<name_for_labels>>
  #| echo: false
  if (is.null(val_dat$PBreg[[<<i>>]])) {
    cat("Not enough data for Passing Bablok regression.")
  } else {
      plot_title <- paste0("Test: ", val_dat$Analyt[[<<i>>]])
      
      # Set up the layout for 3 plots side by side
      # par(mfrow = c(1, 3))
      
      # First plot: Passing Bablok
      MCResult.plot(val_dat$PBreg[[<<i>>]],
                  equal.axis = TRUE,
                  points.col = "#68228B",
                  points.pch = 19, ci.area = TRUE,
                  ci.area.col = "#0000FF50",
                  main = plot_title,
                  sub = "",
                  add.cor = TRUE,
                  cor.method = "spearman",
                  add.grid = FALSE,
                  points.cex = 1)

      ##Angabe Steigung und Achsenabschnitt und CI
      intercept_est <- val_dat$PBreg[[<<i>>]]@para[1]
      intercept_lci <- val_dat$PBreg[[<<i>>]]@para[5]
      intercept_uci <- val_dat$PBreg[[<<i>>]]@para[7]
      gradient_est <- val_dat$PBreg[[<<i>>]]@para[2]
      gradient_lci <- val_dat$PBreg[[<<i>>]]@para[6]
      gradient_uci <- val_dat$PBreg[[<<i>>]]@para[8]
      alpha_ci <- val_dat$PBreg[[<<i>>]]@alpha[1]
      text(cex=.65,
        x=max(val_dat$data[[<<i>>]][,1:2])*0.8,y=max(val_dat$data[[<<i>>]][,1:2])*0.49,
          sprintf("Gradient : %4.2f (%4.2f - %4.2f)", 
            gradient_est, 
            gradient_lci, 
            gradient_uci))
      text(cex=.65,
        x=max(val_dat$data[[<<i>>]][,1:2])*0.8,y=max(val_dat$data[[<<i>>]][,1:2])*0.42,
          sprintf("Intercept : %4.2f (%4.2f - %4.2f)", 
            intercept_est, 
            intercept_lci, 
            intercept_uci))
      text(cex=.65,
        x=max(val_dat$data[[<<i>>]][,1:2])*0.8,y=max(val_dat$data[[<<i>>]][,1:2])*0.35, 
          sprintf("alpha : %4.2f", 
            alpha_ci))
            
      fitPaBa <- mcreg(as.matrix(val_dat$data[[<<i>>]][,1:2]), method.reg="PaBa", na.rm=TRUE)
      fitlr <- mcreg(as.matrix(val_dat$data[[<<i>>]][,1:2]), method.reg="LinReg", na.rm=TRUE)
      
      # Second and third plots: comparing intercetp and slope
      compareFit(fitlr, fitPaBa)      

  }
  ```',
  .open = "<<",
  .close = ">>"
  )
  
  output_panel_blandaltman <- glue(
    '
  #### Bland-Altman
  ```{r}
  #| label: plot-blandaltman-<<name_for_labels>>
  #| echo: false
  if (is.null(val_dat$PBreg[[<<i>>]])) {
    cat("Not enough data for Bland-Altman plot.")
  } else {
      MCResult.plotDifference(val_dat$PBreg[[<<i>>]], main = plot_title)
      MCResult.plotDifference(val_dat$PBreg[[<<i>>]], plot.type = 8, main = paste("rel Difference plot", plot_title))
  }
  ```',
  .open = "<<",
  .close = ">>"
  )
  
  output_panel_datatable <- glue(
    '
  #### Messdaten
  ```{r}
  #| label: data-<<name_for_labels>>
  #| echo: false
  #| message: false
  #| warning: false
  
  val_dat$data[[<<i>>]] |> 
    mutate(DxI800 = round(DxI800, 2),
           DxI9000 = round(DxI9000, 2)) |>
    arrange(Probennummer) |>
    flextable() |>  
    theme_vanilla() |>  
    bg(bg = "grey", part = "header") |> 
    align(align = "center", part = "all") |> 
    bg(j = 4, bg = scales::col_numeric(palette = c("blue", "green", "red"), domain = c(-40, 40))) |> 
    set_table_properties(width = 0.6, layout = "autofit") |> 
    colformat_num(j =5, big.mark = "")
  ```',
  .open = "<<",
  .close = ">>"
  )
 
  output_panel_QCtable <- glue(
    '
  #### QC-Daten
  ```{r}
  #| label: QC-<<name_for_labels>>
  #| echo: false
  #| message: false
  #| warning: false
  
  if (is.null(val_dat$prc.L.raw.data[[<<i>>]])) {
    cat("Not enough data for QC table.")
  } else {
    cat("Level 1")
    val_dat$prc.L.raw.data[[<<i>>]] |> 
      flextable()|> 
      align(align = "center", part = "all")|> 
      autofit()|>
      add_footer_lines("")|>
      bg(bg = "grey", part = "header")
  }
  
  if (is.null(val_dat$prc.H.raw.data[[<<i>>]])) {
    cat("Not enough data for QC table.")
  } else {
    cat("Level 2")
    val_dat$prc.H.raw.data[[<<i>>]] |> 
      flextable()|> 
      align(align = "center", part = "all")|> 
      autofit()|>
      add_footer_lines("")|>
      bg(bg = "grey", part = "header")
  }
  
  ```',
  .open = "<<",
  .close = ">>"
  )
  
  
  # Combine all the pieces
  output <- glue(
    '
  {output_first_part}

  ::: {{.panel-tabset}}
  {output_panel_summary}
  
  {output_panel_plot}

  {output_panel_paba}
  
  {output_panel_blandaltman}
  
  {output_panel_datatable}
  
  {output_panel_QCtable}
  :::'
  )
}
```

```{r, valreports}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| echo: false

# Generierung der Panels
val_reports <- map_chr(
  seq_len(nrow(val_dat)), 
  \(i) build_val_report(i)
)
```

## Appendix
Data is processed using R language^1^, DBI^2^, RSQLite^3^, tidyverse^4^, mcr package^5^, CLSIEP15^6^ and flextable package^7^. glue^8^, knitr^9^ and quarto^10^ are used for converting results into Word, PDF and HTML files. This project was inspired by Daniel Holmes (UBC, CA)^11^, Burak Bahar (Washington, USA)^12^, David Gohel (Roubaix, F)^13^ and Andrew Heiss (Georgia State University, USA)^14^.
  
### References and packages
  
1.  R: A language and environment for statistical computing. R Foundation for Statistical Computing, Vienna, Austria. Version: `r getRversion()` URL: <https://www.R-project.org>
2. DBI: R Database Interface. Version: `r packageDescription("DBI")$Version` URL: <http://CRAN.R-project.org/package=DBI>
3. RSQLite: SQLite Interface for R. Version: `r packageDescription("RSQLite")$Version` URL: <http://CRAN.R-project.org/package=RSQLite>
4.  tidyverse: Easily Install and Load the 'Tidyverse'. Version: `r packageDescription("tidyverse")$Version` URL: <http://CRAN.R-project.org/package=tidyverse>
5.  mcr: Method Comparison Regression. Version: `r packageDescription("mcr")$Version` URL: <http://CRAN.R-project.org/package=mcr>
6.  CLSIEP15: Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute (CLSI) EP15-A3 Calculations. Version: `r packageDescription("CLSIEP15")$Version` URL: <http://CRAN.R-project.org/package=CLSIEP15>
7.  flextable: a framework for easily creating tables. Version: `r packageDescription("flextable")$Version` URL: <http://CRAN.R-project.org/package=flextable>
8.  glue: Interpreted String Literals. Version: `r packageDescription("glue")$Version` URL: <http://CRAN.R-project.org/package=glue>
9.  knitr: A General-Purpose Package for Dynamic Report Generation in R. Version: `r packageDescription("knitr")$Version` URL: <http://yihui.org/knitr>
10.  quarto: Quarto: Open-Source Scientific and Technical Publishing System. Version: `r packageDescription("quarto")$Version` URL: <https://quarto.org>
11.  The Lab-R-torian: URL: <https://labrtorian.com/>
12.  An interactive website for analytical method comparison and bias estimation: URL: <https://bahar.shinyapps.io/method_compare/>
13.  SOLUTIONS ET FORMATIONS EN DATA-SCIENCE: URL: <https://www.ardata.fr/>
